questions.q: Let $f_{k}(x)=\frac{1}{k}  \left(\sin ^{k}x+\cos ^{k} x\right)$ for $\mathrm{k}=1,2,3, \ldots$ Then for all $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R},$the value of $f_{4}(x)-f_{6}(x) is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $f_{k}(x)=\frac{1}{k}\left(\sin ^{k} x+\cos ^{k} x\right)f_{4}(x)=\frac{1}{4}\left[\sin ^{4} x+\cos ^{4} x\right]=\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(\sin ^{2} x+\cos ^{2} x\right)^{2}-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{2}\right]=\frac{1}{4}\left[1-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{2}\right]f_{6}(x)=\frac{1}{6}\left[\sin ^{6} x+\cos ^{6} x\right]=\frac{1}{6}\left[\left(\sin ^{2} x+\left(\cos ^{2} x\right)-\frac{3}{4}  \left(\sin ^{2}x\right)^{2}\right]\right.$=\frac{1}{6}\llleft[1-\frac{3}{4}(\sin$2 x)^{2}\right]$ Now f_{4}(x)-f_{(6)}(x)=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6}-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{8}+\frac{1}{8}(\sin$2 x)^{2}=\frac{1}{12}$

questions.q: Let $|\cos \theta \cos (60-\theta) \cos (60+\theta)| \leq \frac{1}{8}, \theta \epsilon[0,2 \pi]$. Then, the sum of all $\theta \epsilon[0,2 \pi]$, where $\cos 3 \theta$ attains its maximum value, is :

questions.solution:
We know that
$(\cos \theta)\left(\cos( 6 0 ^ { {}^{{}^{\circ}} } - \theta ) \left(\cos \left(60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}+\theta\right)=\frac{1}{4} \cos 3 \theta\right.\right.$
So equation reduces to \left|\frac{1}{4} \cos 3 \theta\right| \leq \frac{1}{8}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow|\cos 3 \theta| \leq \frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{2} \leq \cos 3 \theta \leq \frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ maximum value of $\cos 3 \theta=\frac{1}{2}$, here
$\begin{aligned}

Whose sum is
$\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{5 \pi}{9}+\frac{7 \pi}{9}+\frac{11 \pi}{9}+\frac{13 \pi}{9}+\frac{17 \pi}{9}=\frac{54 \pi}{9}=6 \pi

questions.q: $96cos\dfrac{π}{33}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{33}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{33}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{33}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{33}$& is equal to&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Expression& $96 \cdot cos\dfrac{π}{33} \cdot cos\dfrac{2\pi}{33} \cdot cos\dfrac{4\pi}{33} . . . . . . . . . cos\dfrac{16\pi}{33}$

Now we know that,

$cosA \cdot cos2A \cdot cos{2}^{2}A \cdot cos{2}^{3}A . . . . . \cdot cos{2}^{n - 1}A = \dfrac{sin{2}^{n}A}{{2}^{n}sinA}$

Now using the above formula in given expression we get,

$96 \cdot cos\dfrac{π}{33} \cdot cos\dfrac{2\pi}{33} \cdot cos\dfrac{4\pi}{33} . . . . . . . . . cos\dfrac{16\pi}{33}$

$= 96 \times \dfrac{sin\dfrac{32\pi}{33}}{{2}^{5}sin\dfrac{π}{33}}$

$= 96 \times \dfrac{sin\left(\pi - \dfrac{π}{33}\right)}{{2}^{5}sin\dfrac{π}{33}}$

$= 96 \times \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{π}{33}\right)}{{2}^{5}sin\dfrac{π}{33}}\left\{\text{as}sin\left(\pi - \alpha\right) = sin\alpha\right\}$

$= 96 \times \dfrac{1}{32} = 3$

questions.q: If $tan15 ° + \dfrac{1}{tan75 °} + \dfrac{1}{tan105 °} + tan195 ° = 2a$, then the value of  \left(a + \dfrac{1}{a}\right)$ is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$2a = tan15 ° + \dfrac{1}{tan75 °} + \dfrac{1}{tan105 °} + tan195 °$

$⇒ 2a = tan15 ° + \dfrac{1}{tan \left(90 ° - 15 °\right)} + $\dfrac{1}{tan\left(90 ° + 15 °\right)} ++$tan\left($180 ° + 15 °\right)$

$⇒ 2a = tan15 ° + \dfrac{1}{cot15 °} - \dfrac{1}{cot15 °} +tan15 °$

$⇒ 2a = 2tan15 °$

$⇒ a = tan15 °$

$⇒ a = tan \left($45 ° - 30 °\right)$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{3}}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

So,

$a + \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$

$⇒ a + \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)2}{2}$

$⇒ a + \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{8}{2} =4$

questions.q: The value of $2sin\dfrac{π}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $2sin\dfrac{π}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

Now by we know that~$sin \left(\theta\right) =cos \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \theta\right), so by using this we get~sin\dfrac{π}{22} =cos\left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{π}{22}\right) =cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11}~and similarly~sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22} =cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11},sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22} =cos\dfrac{3\pi}{11},sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22} = \dfrac{2\pi}{11},sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22} =cos\dfrac{π}{11}

So,~2sin\dfrac{π}}{22}sin\dfrac{3\p$p$pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\p$p$pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\p$p$pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{5\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{3\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{1\pi}{11}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{1\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\p$p$pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

{As~$cos\dfrac{3\pi}{22} = --cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{11}\right) = --cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}$and $cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11} = --cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}

$= $\dfrac{2sin\dfrac{π}{11}}{2sin\dfrac{π}}}{11}}cos\dfrac{π}}{11}cos\dfrac{2\ppi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pppi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pppi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{2}sin\dfrac{π}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{3}sin\dfrac{π}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{16\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}}{{2}^{4}sin\dfrac{π}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{sin\dfrac{32\pi}{11}}{{2}^{4}sin\dfrac{π}{11}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{16}\dfrac{sin\left(3\pi - \dfrac{π}{11}\right)}{sin\dfrac{π}{11}} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

$= 27\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\right)3 + 8\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}\right)3$

$= 250$

$
